# Register workers

Before a worker can proxy sessions, it must register with a Boundary controller.
Registration establishes the worker as a resource in the `global` scope and creates the credentials the worker uses to authenticate to its upstream.

All workers use certificates and encryption keys to identify themselves and to protect data in transit.
Boundary supports three registration methods so that you can fit worker registration into any workflow.
The controller-led and worker-led methods are token-based: the worker presents a token that a controller authorizes.
The external KMS method is KMS-based: the worker authenticates with a KMS key that it shares with its upstream.

## Compare the registration methods

| Method | How it works | Requires an API call | Requires `auth_storage_path` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Controller-led](/boundary/docs/workers/registration/controller-led) | You generate an activation token on the controller, then place it in the worker configuration file. | Yes, before you start the worker | Yes |
| [Worker-led](/boundary/docs/workers/registration/worker-led) | The worker generates a registration request, and you submit it to the controller. | Yes, after you start the worker | Yes |
| [External KMS](/boundary/docs/workers/registration/kms) | The worker authenticates using a KMS key that it shares with its upstream. | No | No |

Use the following guidance to choose a method:

- **Controller-led** works well when you provision workers using a configuration management tool or an instance template, because you can inject the activation token when you render the configuration file.
- **Worker-led** works well when an operator brings a worker online manually, or when the system that provisions the worker cannot reach the Boundary API.
- **External KMS** works well for automatic scaling, because workers register themselves with no operator action. KMS registration does not require workers to store credentials locally.

## Credential storage

Workers that use the controller-led or worker-led methods store their credentials on disk in the directory you define with `auth_storage_path`.
Boundary rotates these credentials automatically.
Do not share an `auth_storage_path` directory between workers.

By default, Boundary does not encrypt the credentials it stores on disk.
You can encrypt them by adding a `kms` block with the `worker-auth-storage` purpose to the worker configuration file:

```hcl
kms "awskms" {
  purpose    = "worker-auth-storage"
  region     = "us-east-1"
  kms_key_id = "19ec80b0-dfdd-4d97-8164-c6examplekey5"
}
```

HashiCorp recommends that you configure a `worker-auth-storage` key for any worker that uses the controller-led or worker-led method.

Workers that register through an external KMS do not require an `auth_storage_path`, because they store their credentials in memory and generate new ones on restart.

## Register downstream workers

In a [multi-hop deployment](/boundary/docs/workers/multi-hop), a downstream worker connects to an upstream worker instead of connecting directly to a controller.
Downstream workers can use any of the registration methods described on this page.
The upstream worker passes the registration request up the chain to the controller, so a downstream worker does not require network access to the control plane.

The `downstream-worker-auth` KMS purpose and token-based registration are compatible.
You configure `downstream-worker-auth` on an upstream worker so that it can authenticate downstream workers that register through an external KMS.
That configuration does not prevent the same upstream worker from passing token-based requests from other downstream workers to the controller.
A single upstream worker can serve downstream workers that use the controller-led, worker-led, and external KMS methods at the same time.

The upstream worker itself can also register by token.
If the upstream worker has a `downstream-worker-auth` block and no `worker-auth` block, it registers with the controller using the controller-led or worker-led method.

<Note>

  A worker cannot combine token-based registration with a `worker-auth` KMS block.
  If a worker configuration has a `worker-auth` block and also sets `controller_generated_activation_token` or `auth_storage_path`, Boundary fails to start the worker.
  To register a worker using a token, do not configure a `worker-auth` block on that worker.

</Note>

To use a separate KMS trust domain for downstream workers, refer to [Authenticate downstream workers](/boundary/docs/workers/multi-hop/downstream-worker-auth).
